info.name: Globie Keeper
info.description:
End-to-end walkthrough of the Globie Keeper API (agreement-first group-bill reimbursement).

**Run order**: Health → Auth → Seeded demo → Agent tools → Full create flow → NEAR settlement.

**Before running**

1. `docker compose up -d db` then `npm --prefix server run seed` (seed is explicit, never part of deploy).
2. Start the API: `npm --prefix server run dev` (defaults to `http://localhost:3001`).
3. Import `local.postman_environment.json` and select it.

**What works without any credentials**

Folders 01–03 run against the deterministic seed: group `KHAOSI`, one 1 200.00 THB bill split Ana 445.00 / Ben 400.00 / Chai 355.00, Ana already paid on NEAR (10 Globie, rank 1), Ben `requested`, Chai `confirmed`. Every request in folders 01–03 is ordinary HTTP; settling a share is the one step that needs a real NEP-141 transfer hash, because the server verifies the receipt on chain and has no unsigned path.

**What needs credentials**

- Folder 04 stops being meaningful after `POST /bills/:id/parse` unless `NEAR_AI_API_KEY` (NEAR AI Cloud) is set: the extractor returns no draft, the bill falls back to `UPLOADED` and `PATCH /bills/:id/allocations` answers 409 `bill_empty`. Set `receiptPath` to a photo of a real receipt first.
- Folder 05 needs NEAR configured (`NEAR_NETWORK` plus the network's `NEAR_USDC_CONTRACT`) and a linked NEAR account on the paying member and the fronter. Without the contract the NEAR routes answer 409 `near_not_configured` and move no money.

Every collection variable (`anaToken`, `billId`, `benShareId`, …) is filled in by earlier requests, so a full run needs no manual copying — except the three bearer tokens in folder 01, which only a NEAR wallet can mint and must be pasted in once.

item.name: 00 · Health
item.description: Cheap liveness probe. The same handler is mounted at `/health` (container healthcheck) and `/api/health` (through the proxy).

item.name: 01 · Auth
item.description: NEAR sign-in is the only credential — there is no email or password route. `POST /auth/near/nonce` mints a challenge, the wallet signs it, and `POST /auth/near/verify` returns the opaque 60-day bearer token (see folder 01b). Postman cannot sign, so paste the three demo bearer tokens into `anaToken` / `benToken` / `chaiToken` once — copy them from the app after signing in as each persona, or mint one per persona through folder 01b. The requests below only confirm each token still resolves to the right person.

request.description: Set `anaToken` first: sign in as Ana with a NEAR wallet and copy `token` out of the app's `localStorage['globie.session']`.

item.name: 01b · Log in with NEAR (optional)
item.description: NEP-413 sign-in — the only wallet login this app offers. Two steps: `POST /auth/near/nonce` mints a challenge, the wallet signs it, `POST /auth/near/verify` checks the ed25519 signature and that the key is FullAccess on the account. No password, no OAuth client, no signing key on the server.

exec: pm.test('a nonce, the exact message to sign, and the recipient', () => {

request.description: `accountId` is optional — a wallet picker decides the account. Only the hash of the nonce is stored, so a leaked row cannot be replayed. The returned `message` is what the wallet must sign verbatim.

item.name: Verify with a forged signature — refused

request.description: The nonce is real and fresh, the signature is 64 zero bytes, so `verifySignedMessage` answers 401 `near_login_bad_signature`. A key that is not on the account answers 401 `near_login_key_not_found`; a malformed key answers 400 `near_login_bad_public_key`. The nonce is spent either way, so re-run request 1 before trying again.

exec: pm.test('a normal bearer session comes back', () => {

request.description: Re-run request 1 so `nearNonce` is fresh (request 2 spends its own), sign the returned `message` with a FullAccess ed25519 key on `nearAccountId`, then paste the base58 key into `nearPublicKey` and the base64 signature into `nearSignature`. The reply is the same 60-day session the app signs in with.

item.description: Reads the deterministic seed. There is no `GET /groups` list route, so the collection resolves ids by joining with the seeded invite code `KHAOSI` — the endpoint is idempotent for members who already belong.

item.name: 03 · Agent tools
item.description: The §2.11 contract. Four tools move money or message people, so they answer with a confirmation challenge first; replaying the identical body with the returned `confirmToken` executes. Tokens are bound to the member, the tool and a SHA-256 of the canonical args, and expire after 10 minutes.

item.name: Settle Ben's share on NEAR (needs a real transfer)

exec: pm.test('Globie was awarded on first settlement', () => {

request.description: Set `settlementTxHash` to the hash of an `ft_transfer` Ben really sent to `globie-ana.testnet` for exactly 400.00 THB worth of the configured USDC contract. The server re-reads the receipt and checks sender, token, receiver and amount — a wrong value answers 409 `near_tx_*`, and an empty variable answers 409 `near_tx_not_found` or `near_not_configured`. Nothing becomes paid on this rail without a verified receipt.

item.name: 04 · Full create flow (needs NEAR_AI_API_KEY)
item.description:
Creates a brand new group so the seeded agreement does not collide (`409 agreement_active`). Everything up to `PATCH /bills/:id/allocations` runs without credentials; the parse step only produces line items when `NEAR_AI_API_KEY` is configured — otherwise the bill falls back to `UPLOADED` with a warning and the allocation step answers `409 bill_empty`.

Set `receiptPath` to a photo of a real receipt before running, and give the request an explicit file path in the body tab if Postman cannot resolve the variable.

exec: pm.test('everyone agreed — the agreement is accepted', () => pm.expect(body.agreement.status).to.eql('accepted'));

request.description: The file part must be named `file`; `kind` is optional and inferred from the MIME type. 25 MB limit, one file per request.
Returns before the vision call finishes. Without `NEAR_AI_API_KEY` the extractor produces no draft and the bill drops back to `UPLOADED` with a warning.

item.name: 05 · NEAR settlement (optional)
item.description: Real settlement on NEAR. Needs `NEAR_NETWORK` and that network's `NEAR_USDC_CONTRACT`, plus a NEAR account on the paying member and on the fronter. Without the contract every route here answers 409 `near_not_configured`; with it, a share still only becomes paid once a real `ft_transfer` hash is verified on chain.

pm.test('the instruction names the fronter as payee', () => {

request.description: Fronter only, and only while the bill is FINALIZED or COLLECTING. Idempotent: the memo is the share id, so re-requesting resumes the same transfer instead of creating a second one — `alreadyRequested` says which. Answers 409 `fronter_near_missing` / `member_near_missing` when either side has no linked account.
